clue.text: Instrument cut a part of the eye

indicators.note: cut says the word for the instrument loses its final letter

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument like a small trumpet

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is cut down to size, followed by a reference to anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the last letter of the brass instrument's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The transparent dome over the iris and pupil is a named part of the eyeball.

clue.text: Unusual way in which leader gets demoted

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for way is moved further down the column, in this down clue to the end

parts.note: a route is a way to go

explanation.surface: An odd arrangement in which the boss is moved to a lower rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader gets demoted' sends the R of ROUTE from the top to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré is a borrowing from French meaning eccentric or beyond the bounds of the normal.

clue.text: A snorter, close to hurricane winds?

definitions.text: A snorter, close to hurricane winds?

indicators.note: winds is read as the verb, twisting the letters of the preceding words around
close to means the end letter of hurricane

explanation.surface: A real snorter of a gale, almost hurricane strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' twists A SNORTER plus E (the last letter of hurricane, from 'close to') into the answer; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong gale blowing from the north-east is a fierce storm, nearly a hurricane in force.

clue.text: Oscar supports a vote for handsome chap

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter for Oscar sits underneath, holding up the rest

parts.note: a poll is a vote
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner backs a ballot for a good-looking man.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god famed for his beauty gives his name to any very handsome young man.

clue.text: Doctor at Bart's called firstly for summary

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are rearranged
firstly takes only the opening letter of called

explanation.surface: A doctor at St Bart's hospital was called first to give a summary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but rearranges ATBARTS plus C (from 'firstly'). Bart's is St Bartholomew's, a London hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short précis of a paper or report, setting out its main points.

clue.text: Pan Tory cryptically suggesting desperate measure?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the words any port, stormed (shuffled), give the letters of these two clue words

explanation.surface: Criticising the Conservatives across the board seems a desperate step.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: PAN TORY is what you get when ANY PORT is put in a 'storm', an anagram. The phrase means taking whatever refuge is available.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb describes accepting any help or refuge in a crisis, so a desperate expedient.

clue.text: Malicious woman from Slough turned up last

parts.note: to slough is to shed, as a snake does its skin

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the word for last is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to last is to live on, survive

explanation.surface: A spiteful woman from the town of Slough showed up at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slough' poses as the Berkshire town, west of London, but is the verb. 'turned up' flips LIVE to EVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicious, spiteful woman is called a fiend of her sex, a female demon.

clue.text: First person embraced by Australian animal lover

indicators.note: embraced by means the pronoun goes inside the animal's name

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo
me is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone hugged by a kangaroo becomes an animal lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'animal lover' looks like one phrase; the definition is just 'lover'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero of Verona has become the byword for an ardent male suitor.

clue.text: Virtuous group saving Government

indicators.note: saving means except, so the abbreviation is left out

parts.note: a contingent is a group, as of troops

explanation.surface: A high-minded faction rescues the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' looks like rescuing but means 'except', removing G.
explanation.definitionFit: Continent here means self-restrained, especially sexually chaste, so morally upright.

clue.text: Conventional image of hi-fi enthusiast?

definitions.meaning: a fixed, oversimplified idea of a kind of person or thing
read as two words, a sound-system kind of person: a fan of record players and speakers

explanation.surface: A cliché picture of the typical audio buff.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word: a stereo system plus 'type' for a sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A stereotype is a standardised mental picture held in common about a group.

clue.text: Mark keeps wearing fur

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the abbreviation surrounds the other letters

parts.note: MK is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
you are in clothes you are wearing

explanation.surface: Mark is still dressed in his fur coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of this small weasel-like mammal is prized for luxury coats.

clue.text: Group of women extremely eager to stop backing fossil fuels

indicators.note: to stop is to plug, so the end letters go into the reversed fuels
backing means the two fuel words are written backwards

parts.note: oil and gas are both fossil fuels

indicators.note: extremely takes the outside letters of eager

explanation.surface: A women's group is very keen to halt support for coal, oil and gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the two fuels written as one word; the outer letters of eager, from 'extremely', go in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a harem, the women's quarters of a Muslim household and those who live there.

clue.text: Titillating books penned by Blair?

indicators.note: penned by means held inside, as in a pen

parts.note: Eric Blair was the real name of George Orwell
OT is the Old Testament, a group of books

explanation.surface: Racy books written by Blair, the former Prime Minister?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blair' suggests Tony Blair, but it is Eric Blair, Orwell's real name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sexually arousing is titillating, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Join a clumsy ship going to port?

indicators.note: port is the left side, so in this across clue the boat's word travels right to left

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: Boarding an old tub heading for harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like a harbour but means leftwards, reversing TUB to BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To border on or touch along an edge is to adjoin, sharing a boundary.

clue.text: Billion offered originally to housing fund — not half generous!

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of offered
housing means containing, so the half word goes inside

parts.note: until means up to, as in open to nine

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first two letters of fund

explanation.surface: A billion offered to a housing fund: generous, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is the British exclamation meaning 'and how!', but here it halves the word fund.
explanation.definitionFit: Bountiful means giving freely and liberally, the same as generous.

clue.text: They had three banks, note, blocking attempts involving mortgage initially

indicators.note: blocking means the note gets in the way, inside the attempts
involving says the attempts take in the mortgage initial as well, so both pieces end up inside

parts.note: tries are attempts
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of mortgage

explanation.surface: A sentence about bank lending tangled up with mortgage applications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests lenders but means the rows of oars on an ancient galley.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Greek warships had three tiers of oarsmen, each tier called a bank.

clue.text: Bedcover that is returned could be red and blue

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation is written backwards

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: could be says the letters of red might become another arrangement

parts.note: down means sad or blue

explanation.surface: A bedspread that, sent back, might be red and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives EI; 'could be' rearranges RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with soft feathers from a sea duck serves as a warm bedcover.

clue.text: Jockey is around? He's an old-fashioned sort

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre, shifting these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A jockey hangs around the yard, a traditional type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jockey' looks like a rider but is the verb, rearranging ISAROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hopelessly out of date is figuratively called a prehistoric reptile, a relic.

clue.text: Airport in New York, not LA, needs new curator

indicators.note: not means the letters LA are dropped

parts.note: LaGuardia is one of New York City's airports

explanation.surface: A New York airport, not Los Angeles, needs a new manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is a keeper or custodian, someone in charge of protecting a collection.

clue.text: Ideas that regularly ignored facts

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is skipped, leaving the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Notions that routinely disregarded the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Information gathered for reference or analysis is a set of facts and figures.

clue.text: Sport gets endless criticism, that's plain

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: stick is informal British for criticism, as in taking stick

explanation.surface: A sport that keeps being criticised, plain and simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' is British slang for harsh criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means simple and unsophisticated, in the manner of the countryside.

clue.text: Among loves, count opera

indicators.note: among puts the word for count between the two letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O, so two loves give two Os
to tell is to count, as a teller counts votes

explanation.surface: A count sits among his sweethearts at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' poses as a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's opera based on Othello is one specific example of an opera.

clue.text: Song of some heavenly riches

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hymn about the treasures of heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of a song are its lyric, and a short songlike poem goes by the same name.

clue.text: One sits in second row, ignoring a hoarder

indicators.note: sits in means the numeral is placed inside
ignoring means the letter a is dropped

parts.note: a row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone sits in the second row of seats, ignoring a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line of seats but means an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: This rodent buries nuts for winter, so a person who stockpiles things is one.

clue.text: Subtract a quarter from lower number

indicators.note: subtract says the compass letter is taken away

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction: take a fraction from a smaller figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but something that numbs, read as NUMB-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The old anaesthetic deadens feeling, so it is a numbing agent.

clue.text: American pilots retreating to a distance

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a body of pilots

explanation.surface: American airmen pulling back to a safe range.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a great way off, a long way away.

clue.text: A greengrocer's uses one rightly, and wrongly too perhaps?

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of the following words are put in the wrong order

parts.note: the clue's own possessive needs the punctuation mark correctly, while a shop sign like potato's misuses it, the famous greengrocer's error

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper uses a punctuation mark correctly here, and perhaps incorrectly too.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'greengrocer's apostrophe' is the British name for a stray apostrophe in plurals on shop signs, such as 'banana's'; the clue's own possessive uses one correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark showing possession appears correctly in the clue's own possessive word.

clue.text: Pick fruit around English coast on vacation, right?

indicators.note: around means the fruit wraps the other letters

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of coast remain

explanation.surface: Picking fruit around the English coast while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick' looks like a verb but is the guitar sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A small piece of plastic for strumming a guitar is called a pick.

clue.text: Singer from California, not American

parts.note: nary is an American dialect word meaning not one, as in nary a word

explanation.surface: A vocalist from California, though not American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not American' is a single phrase defining NARY, not a removal of A.
explanation.definitionFit: The canary is a songbird, and singer is a crossword staple for one.
